title: Gradient Shield: Traffic Warden for Canary Scheduling
creator: Priya Nandakumar
description: Purpose: Build a policy engine (Traffic Warden) that expresses canary/A-B/shadow campaigns as composable 'gradient' plans: a sequence of timed or metric-driven steps that compute traffic splits, shadow percentages, and fallback rules. The engine must support: 1) declarative step schedules (time-based, metric-based), 2) fractional traffic arithmetic (weighted splits across variants and cohorts), 3) shadow probes with configurable sampling and target duplications, 4) flexible guardrails (latency/regression thresholds, error-rate gates, cost caps) and 5) automated rollback and remediation actions (rollback, pause, scale-up, notify). This ticket covers spec, control-plane schema, runtime decision hooks, basic telemetry events and a reference implementation that integrates with the existing rollout controller API.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Policy DSL: JSON/YAML schema published and validated by unit tests; supports time-based steps, metric predicates, and cohort selectors.
2) Runtime: Controller can evaluate a stored policy and emit per-request routing decisions (primary vs variant vs shadow) with <2ms median decision latency in local bench.
3) Guardrails: Engine wires into telemetry to stop or rollback when SLO regressions exceed thresholds (latency p95 +5%, error rate +1%).
4) Rollback: Automated rollback path triggers a safe rollback and an annotated incident with root-cause pointers.
5) Observability: Events emitted for each step transition, guardrail trip, shadow sample, and rollback. Dashboards show rollout progression and per-cohort metrics.
